summary: Indio sits on the floor of the Coachella Valley, a vast desert basin flanked by the San Jacinto and Little San Bernardino mountain ranges, which means sunset views here aren't gentle fades — they're high-contrast spectacles of pink and orange light bouncing off bare rock faces to the west. The city is perhaps best known as the host of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, held annually at the Empire Polo Club, an event that temporarily makes this community of roughly 93,000 one of the most watched spots on earth — then hands it back to its quieter default rhythm. That rhythm is shaped by agriculture, hospitality, and healthcare: date palm groves still line stretches of Highway 111, and the broader valley's resort and medical infrastructure provides a significant share of local jobs, though many residents commute west toward Palm Desert or Palm Springs. At a median home price of about $425,000 against a median household income near $79,000, the price-to-income ratio lands around 5.4 — meaningfully more accessible than coastal California but still a stretch that likely pushes many households toward renting at roughly $1,400 a month. The climate is unambiguous: an annual average daily high of 86°F and over ten hours of sunshine per day mean summer heat is genuinely intense, while winters are warm and dry enough to make outdoor activity a year-round consideration — the Coachella Valley trail system and nearby Joshua Tree National Park sit within easy reach. Indio is a place defined by the tension between its global brand recognition for a single weekend each April and the sprawling, car-dependent desert city that exists the other 51 weeks.
